rationale: The thesis-derived paper and grant project were identified, but the full fatigue model remains unrecovered. Secondary total and subscale MFIS values have little change overall. No refined canola-only or Parkinson fatigue effect is isolated.

Published aggregate PBA-s has no reported between-group difference and no numerical table. Both arms switch after six months. The supplement and a separate apathy-item estimate remain inaccessible; safflower processing was unreported.

The Japanese choking series cannot link its shiitake case to a diagnosed person. The modern FEES recipes vary in texture and composition. A separate public interview reports eating difficulty with unknown preparation and no measured swallowing outcome.

Both original Europe PMC pairs are now reviewed. Oral fruit powder and chewed-seed uses are reported without measured responses. The crude-extract animal behavior and ordinary powder edema study measure different outcomes and leave a culinary Parkinson pain comparison open. The powder-group method and result table remain unrecovered.

The registry and thesis specify a force-platform balance assessment. The full thesis tables and journal report lack a verified comparative balance result. The intervention is a supplement and exercise, with no steamed spinach or Parkinson balance comparison.
